summary: Complete Q1 Explore review of 104 finished with changes-requested. The closed-schema direction correctly replaces the permissive unknown-field channel, but Q1-RE-003 remains unresolved because it makes a review Run require reviewVerdictRef to its own terminal result.json. A content-hash ResultRef embedded in its own hashed file is self-referential and cannot be constructed or verified. Q1-RE-001 also remains open at the broader ResultRef boundary: Core derivation is specified only for context.inputRef, while producedResultRefs, consumedInputRefs, verificationSummaryRef, and reviewVerdictRef remain caller-provided ActionResult fields despite the Q1 reference requiring production fingerprints to be Core-derived.

blockingFindings.title: Core-owned ResultRef provenance remains limited to context.inputRef
blockingFindings.evidence: The Explore correctly makes createRun derive context.inputRef, but section 3.3 identifies the separate defects that ActionResult.consumedInputRefs/producedResultRefs are not derived or checked. Section 4.1 retains all four ActionResult ResultRef categories in the allowlist, while section 4.2-4.3 only defines creation and preflight validation for context.inputRef. Current validateActionResultWithoutRunRef validates caller-provided ResultRef shapes and writeRunResult serializes the caller's object; neither derives fingerprints from the target. The updated reference section 6.5 states that production ResultRef/versionFingerprint must be machine generated, not just the context input reference.
blockingFindings.impact: An author can still fabricate, stale, or misbind produced, consumed, verification, and review ResultRefs in a terminal ActionResult. The closed schema restricts field names but does not establish the required provenance authority, so Q1 would leave a central ResultRef integrity gap unchanged.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Keep Q1-RE-001 open and specify one Core-owned derivation/validation path for every allowed ResultRef category. Callers may provide typed target descriptors or identifiers, never versionFingerprint values; Core resolves each target, computes the canonical fingerprint, constructs the ResultRef, and verifies all referenced targets before terminal publication. Define category-specific allowed targets (Run result, Change verification artifact, reviewer findings artifact), missing/unreadable/replaced-target failures, and tests for all ResultRef categories.

blockingFindings.title: Reviewer-result reference design creates a self-referential content hash
blockingFindings.evidence: Section 4.1 defines reviewVerdictRef as a reference to the review Run's own result.json and requires review-* Runs to carry that reference. ResultRef.versionFingerprint is the SHA-256 of target file content; embedding a reference whose fingerprint is the hash of the very result.json that contains it produces a circular hash equation. C1 already omits only ActionResult.runRef from serialized result.json to avoid this exact self-reference; reviewVerdictRef is not omitted. The allowlist also does not name a formal reviewer-findings field even though it says that result.json carries one.
blockingFindings.impact: No implementation can write a stable, terminal review result satisfying this contract: changing the embedded fingerprint changes the target content and therefore its fingerprint. Treating it as optional would violate the stated requirement; accepting a caller-provided value would violate Q1-RE-001 and version binding.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Keep Q1-RE-003 open. Choose a non-self-referential reviewer result design: either add a closed, typed reviewer-findings/verdict payload directly to the terminal review result and require later non-review consumers to reference that completed result, or create a distinct reviewer-owned findings artifact before result.json and reference that artifact. Do not require a review Run to reference its own result.json. Define the new field/artifact's serialization, atomic lifecycle, ResultRef construction, reader reconstruction, and tests for content-hash stability and stale-result detection.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Explore source links remain checkout-specific
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Code citations still use file:///D:/Projects/flowkit absolute paths, which cannot resolve from a different checkout or platform.
nonBlockingFindings.recommendedResolution: Convert these citations to repository-relative Markdown links during a future in-scope Explore edit. This remains non-blocking because the cited source evidence was independently verified.

resolvedFindings.evidence: Concrete verification scripts remain assigned to F1; Q1 retains only verification timing, ownership, and Full-Test authorization boundaries.
